newsitem.title: GERMANY: Aluminium recycling industry forecasts output rise.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium recycling industry forecasts output rise.

text.p: Economic recovery in 1997 should help boost output at European secondary aluminium smelters after a weaker performance in 1996, the European Aluminium Refiners and Remelters Association (OEA) said.
But an OEA statement received here quoted president Arved von Lewinski as saying higher orders would not necessarily mean better earnings.
"Our industry is doing badly...we will face serious problems unless we cut costs significantly," he said.
A number of factors were depressing OEA members' operating margins, he added.
These were European remelting overcapacity, a flow of scrap away from West Europe to new production centres in South East Asia, Latin America and East Europe, and global foundry sector concentration.
Lewinski said secondary production in Europe in the first half of 1996, at about 800,000 tonnes, was four percent down from the same 1995 period.

Output in the second half of the year had also lagged comparable 1995 levels and output in the full year might be two percent below the 1995 figure of 1.71 million tonnes, the OEA secretariat in Duesseldorf said.
Producers of casting and wrought alloys had become more optimistic in recent weeks because of higher London Metals Exchange prices in tandem with lower aluminium alloy stocks.
OEA represents aluminium recycling across Europe and co-ordinates the interests of scrap-using producers.
The four leading secondary aluminium producers are Germany, Britain, France and Italy.
